forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let n > 1 and let f_n be defined as above. For any real r with 0 <= r < 1, if m = floor(n*r), then f_n(r) <= f_n(m/n).

payload.role_in_assembly: Places r inside the same normalized interval as m/n.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given the earlier hypotheses and assuming n > 0, the inequality m divided by n is at most r, and r is strictly less than (m plus 1) divided by n.

variables.name: n
variables.role: positive divisor used to form the bounds

variables.name: r
variables.role: quantity bounded between two consecutive rationals

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses introduced in the statement; r is taken from earlier hypotheses (definition/constraints not specified here).

payload.statement_nl: Under the same hypotheses, because n > 0 one has m/n <= r < (m + 1)/n.

result_payload.proof_nl: Let m = floor(nr). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer satisfying m <= nr < m + 1. Since n > 1, we have n > 0, so dividing the inequality by the positive number n preserves the inequality signs. Therefore m/n <= r < (m + 1)/n. This is exactly the desired statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: Apply the floor definition to nr, then divide by the positive integer n.
